title: Chapter 8. The Journey through the Northern Country
html:
Virachandra converts the people of the North; the miracle of the storm at Maldah; Durlabha Chhatri, son of Keshava Chhatri, holds a great festival, and Maldah becomes a sripat; the visit to Ekachakra and the founding of Virachandrapur; the journey through Radha (pp. 61–66)

[p. 61]

1I bow to Nityananda, from whose ears hang pearls;
by the power of shelter at his feet one crosses the terrible ocean of samsara.1

2Glory, glory to Baladeva, Nityananda-Rama!
Be merciful, let your qualities and your name shine forth [in me].

3Nityananda Prabhu, my wellspring of mercy,
gave prema for the sake of those who have no way.

4The people of the Northern country are of many kinds:
Shaivas, Shaktas, ritualists, yogis — each with his own customs.

5Their sadhana is wine, meat, fish, chicken […];2
vows to Kamakhya, night vigils [with songs] of Mahipala.

6Festivals and performances of Yogipala and Bhogipala;
all of them dress in Bhotan blankets, sacking and the like.3

7And all these people perform the sankirtana of Hari,
calling aloud, "Nitai! Chaitanya!"

8They worship Radha and Krishna and Vrindavana —
so did Prabhu Virachandra bring them under his rule.

9Such is the merciful Vira avatara:
the wicked, the hostile, the yavanas, all who live badly —

10giving up the nature they had from birth, sing the qualities of Krishna;
so does Virachandra Raya draw them.

11Giving the name of Krishna and bhakti, he delivered them;
such is the avatara Mahaprabhu Virachandra.

12Like the arrows of Kiriti, which bewitch all at once,4
the Lord bound everyone together in the net of his mercy.

13Power, beauty and compassion are his qualities;
they draw the minds of all people.

14On the bank of the Mahananda is a village, Maldah;
there he stopped to rest in the house of a fortunate man.

15It is a domain of the king of Gauda;
many prosperous people live there.

16Seeing him, everyone is amazed;
respectable people say, "This is amorous rasa itself in person!"

17Some say, "This is the Lord himself, embodied and manifest!" —
seeing him full of great radiance without and within.

18How lovely his lotus face, how lovely his smile!
Seeing him manifest, all people are entranced.

19Some say, "Having become compassion embodied,
he fulfils the poor, giving them the wealth of prema."

20And one more wonder they see in his manifestation:
whoever sees him, the name of Krishna comes to his tongue.

21Yavanas, seeing him, come and salute him with a kurnish;
abandoning their own creed, they too say, "Krishna!"

22Every day in every house a festival is held;
all the people became wholehearted Vaishnavas.

23Offering gold coins, jewels, cloth, horses and palanquins,
all the people worshipped him, falling at his feet.

24One day the Lord, in the house of a fortunate man,
was performing sankirtana together with all the Vaishnavas.

25Just then clouds began to gather on every side;
the townspeople grew uneasy at heart.

26The knower of hearts understood everyone's wish:
"Everyone has come to love my kirtan."

[p. 62]

27Storm and rain come on, darkening every quarter,
putting out all the lamps that burn in rows.

28Seeing this, the Lord raised his face and called out:
"Go and pour down outside the compound!

29What joy is there in breaking the joy of the people?
It is the nature of a saint to grieve at another's grief."

30Who has the power to transgress the command of him
whose obedient servants are Brahma, Shiva and the rest?

31Thus restrained,5 the rain falls all around,
but inside the compound neither storm nor rain touches [anyone].

32In bliss all the Vaishnavas perform kirtan;
all cry "Hari, Hari!" with joyful hearts.

33Seeing the Gosai's power, the people stand still
and again and again raise loud cries of Hari's name.

34Inside the compound it is as though a great lamp were burning;
the scent of musk spreads continually.

35Sandal, saffron and flowers fall from above;
a gentle breeze carries [their] fragrance.

36Hearing the sound of the kirtan, all the gods
at once showered down fragrant flowers.

37In the bliss of love for Krishna no one is aware of the outer world —
such is the pastime Prabhu Virachandra Gosai performs.

38For a whole prahara6 rain fell outside the compound;
the fields and squares were filled with water.

39Setting the kirtan aside, the Lord rests,
yet the echo of the kirtan lingers for four dandas.

40Such power did the Lord manifest
that at the sight of him the nature people had from birth went away.

41Whoever sees him says, "Krishna, Hari, Hari!" —
so he drew everyone, the high and the middling.

42From Ramakeli the son of Keshava Chhatri7
came to invite the Lord.

43Many elephants, chariots, horses and palanquins came with him;
leaving them at a distance, he came to the Lord on foot.

44Only one brahmin was with him; all the village people
prostrated themselves by the hundred from afar.

45The Lord said, "Who is this fortunate man?"
All the Vaishnavas called, "Come, come!"

46They informed the Lord, "This is the king's vizier,
the son of Keshava Chhatri, a profound pandit."

47The Lord commanded, "Come closer";
timidly Durlabha Chhatri came near.

48Seeing the Lord's beauty, he was struck still:
it was like the form of Gauranga that [his father] had seen before.

49He saw in him all the same marks —
only that one was a sannyasi, while this one wears cloth tucked in three places.8

50Looking at him, he was amazed at heart
and deemed his own eyes rewarded.

51Prostrating himself, he fell at his feet
and very softly told who he was:

52"Once the Lord came to Ramakeli;
Sri Rupa, Sanatana and my father met [him].9

53Seeing him, they attained the fulfilment of their lives;
to the day of his death my father remembered him.

[p. 63]

54Hearing of this from my father, my mind was filled with longing;
and at the end of last night I saw an auspicious dream.

55Lotus eyes, long arms with armlets,
a gentle smile outshining the full moon.

56He spoke to me very sweet words:
'I shall fulfil what you have desired since birth.

57You long in your heart to see me —
out of mercy to you I have come to your house.

58Look at me to your heart's content,
fill your ears, listening to my kirtan.'

59Saying this to me, the Lord vanished,
and ever since my heart has been restless.

60I am a worldly wretch, yet you have shown such mercy:
with the rope of compassion you have drawn me near.

61You are Chaitanya himself, you are Narayana,
you are Ramachandra, you are the eternal Brahman.

62You are Vishnu, you are Krishna, you are Haladhara,
you are the protector of the three worlds, you are above all.

63In the age of Kali you have shown such mercy to living beings:
by your darshan you have blessed house after house."

64Saying this, he fell at his feet and rolled on the ground;
the Lord accepted him, placing his holy feet on him.

65Again the noble Durlabha made a humble request:
"With your permission, I should like to hold a festival."

66Smiling, the Gosai said, "That is better still!
Everyone, call out loudly, 'Hari, Hari!'"

67Durlabha, overjoyed, went to the town
and began to procure supplies from the shopkeepers.

68Curd, milk, cream skins, chhana, ghee, sugar, molasses,
manda, manohara and pera he brought in abundance;10

69khaja, kshirisa, ganga-jali, khandasar,
sugar, pheni, sugar-candy and more;

70mangoes, jackfruit, coconuts, bananas,
almonds, dried dates, grapes and dates in plenty —

71load upon load he sent to the bank of the Mahananda,
into a fine grove of coconut palms and mangoes.

72Hundreds of people with hoes
cleared the place, making it beautiful.

73Hundreds of new pots were filled with Ganges water,
and bringing it again and again, they all washed the place.

74In the market he bought up [the goods] from the shopkeepers:
"Let each eat whatever he wishes."

75Saying this, he put coins in the shopkeepers' hands,
and they all accepted them with bowed heads.

76He gave orders: "Prepare all the finest foods;
afterwards you will be paid, whatever it comes to.

77Whatever anyone asks for today, I shall pay for;
have no doubt about that.

78As much as each wishes to eat, give him that much;
whatever is asked for, give it, and let it not be otherwise.

79Shopkeepers, all of you go to the edge of the grove;
women, set up stalls at every door.

80However many pilgrims come for darshan,
let each take as much as he wishes, and you shall give it.

81If anyone says, 'I got nothing,' I shall punish [that shopkeeper]:
I shall take all he has and drive him out of the country."

82Hearing this order, everyone was afraid at heart
and at once gave each person whatever he asked for.

83All the poor and wretched, eating and taking [food away],
cried in joy, "Hari bol! Hari bol!"

84All said, "Blessed, blessed is Gosai Mahaprabhu!
Never have we met so kind a Thakura."

[p. 64]

85Some said, "Never have we heard of such a deed";
some said, "It seems the Lord himself has appeared."

86Some said, "This is not within a man's power";
some said, "Krishna, Krishna! Hari, glory, glory!"

87Some said, "We have heard in scripture, in the Bharata,
that King Yudhishthira acted in this way."

88Thus all the people, praising [him],
danced, sang and cried "Hari" at the top of their voices.

89Having arranged everything in this way,
full of prema, [Durlabha] went to the Lord.

90The brahmin cooks who were with the Lord,
having bathed and done their puja, all went [there].

91Each made his own preparations ready;
the kirtan singers began the sankirtana.

92All that was heard was "Hari bol! Hari bol!"
Heaven, earth and the netherworld all answered with the cry "Hari, Hari".

93In bliss auspicious sounds rose to the sky;
all the people gazed with eyes wide open.

94The festival for the arrival of [the Lord], Sri Charana, began;11
all, down to the lowest, sang the qualities of Hari.

95What bliss there was in that village of Maldah!
Everyone said, "We have reached Vaikuntha, the abode of liberation."

96Such power did Virachandra manifest:
millions upon millions of people performed kirtan in bliss.

97Seeing such joy of kirtan in the world of mortals,
Brahma and the other gods came [there].

98Taking human form,12 each with his own retinue,
they all sang kirtan, crying, "Hari bol!"

99Bringing the world of the nagas with him, Vasuki came,
beholding the wondrous pastime of Gaura-Virachandra.

100Taking human form, they all sang kirtan:
"Krishna, Krishna! Rama, Rama! Hari, glory, glory!"

101The world of the gods, the world of men and the world of the nagas, joining together,
performed sankirtana, crying, "O Krishna, Krishna!"

102Such pastimes Gaura Raya performed on earth —
and again, in the form of Virachandra, he floods [the world] with prema.

103Who knows how the Lord performs his pastimes?
Who can understand the ways of the Lord?

104The joy that Vishvambhara once revealed in the city of Navadvipa
together with the devotees and all his associates —

105all that joy appeared in the village of Maldah.
Who can describe it without his mercy?

106The pastimes Virachandra performed out of his own goodness
I have told in brief — only pointing the way.

107Seeing the rich preparations for the kirtan,
Prabhu Virachandra, the essence of the world, smiled.

108Seeing the preparations, the Lord was pleased;
offering [it all] to Krishna, he made it maha-prasada.

109That prasada was carried from place to place,
and each was seated and fed as much as he wished.

110Durlabha received a rare gift — the plate of [the Lord's] remnants —
and, for the sake of his whole lineage, tied it in a cloth and took it away.

111Two thousand coins and a thousand in gold,
two horses from the North and many kinds of cloth,

112and a deed writing over the festival site as devottara,13
he laid before the Lord and, with a cloth round his neck, fell prostrate.

113Showing him mercy, the Lord accepted [the gift]
and said, "This place will become famous."

114From then on Maldah became a sripat14 —
such favour did Virachandra show.

115Taking leave of him, the Lord sent him home
and then made ready to set out for the land of Radha.15

[p. 65]

116On the way, giving prema to all kinds of people,
by stages he came to the town of Ekachakra.

117It is the birthplace of Nityananda Prabhu;
seeing it, he prostrated himself, and prema rose within him.

118Seeing Sri Bankima-deva,16 he was filled with the bliss of prema;
he prostrated himself and offered many hymns of praise.

119How lovely the curve of his face with the flute —
as if one saw the son of the king of Vraja in person!

120Full of prema, the Lord forgot all outward things
and kept saying, "Ah, ah, Krishna, lord of my life!"

121Crying "Nityananda, Nityananda!" he gave loud roars:
"Ah, ah, Gaurachandra Prabhu, son of Shachi!"

122His body bristled like a kadamba flower, streams of tears flowed from his eyes;17
the Lord only kept saying, "Krishna! Hare, Hare!"

123Only after a long while did he grow calm of himself
and very softly spoke composed words:

124"Today fast in this holy place,
and tomorrow morning we shall hold a great festival."

125Taking the order on their heads, all the devotees
performed kirtan whose sound touched the sky.

126All the money there was [from] the journey through the East and the North
he spent, and gathered supplies.

127Rising at dawn, twenty or thirty brahmin cooks
cooked rice, vegetables, dal and the rest.

128Wheat breads and everything fried in ghee,
sweets of kul fruit with honey and with milk,18 many kinds of fruits and roots.

129New clay pots and vessels for water
the potters brought by hundreds of loads.

130Whole, untorn tips of banana leaves,
washed, people brought by thousands upon thousands.

131The place, smeared with cow dung, was exceedingly lovely,
and over it a beautiful canopy.

132On stands the offerings were set in rows,
and on them were placed sprigs of tulasi.

133With his own hands the Lord made the offering,
and Sri Bankima-deva ate with pleasure.

134In great bliss was Prabhu Virachandra Bhagavan;
in bliss all the Vaishnavas performed kirtan.

135The circle of brahmins sat down to eat:
sweets, fried dishes, all kinds of delicacies.

136With his own holy hand [the Lord] served them all;
when they were sated, they could eat no more.19

137All the householder Vaishnavas sat down together
and, sated, cried "Hari" in bliss.

138Having thus completed the festival,
[the Lord] together with his own people took the prasada rice.

139In that village he rested for three days
and named it Virachandrapur.20

140Travelling thus through the land of Radha,
he set out to visit Sri Kundala.21

141In Radha he saw that no one [knew anyone] but Nityananda,
and on people's lips was only the name of Chaitanya.22

142Everyone called out, "Nitai! Chaitanya!
Glory to the sons of Shachi and Padmavati!23

143Glory to Nityananda, glory to Gaurachandra!" —
saying this, they knew no other bliss.

144Holding in their hearts the lotus feet of Radha and Krishna,
immersed in the rasa of prema of Radha and Krishna's pastimes —

145apart from the worship of Radha and Krishna and the Hari-nama,
the people of the land of Radha know nothing else.

146Once Prabhu Nityananda brought them under his rule,
and now Prabhu Virachandra has flooded them with prema.

[p. 66]

147The pastimes of Prabhu Virachandra are the essence of nectar;
whoever hears them with faith becomes one of Gaura's family.

148Hoping for the feet of Sri Jahnava and Nityananda,
Vrindavana Dasa tells the Vamsha-vistara.

Thus ends the eighth chapter of the Vamsha-vistara of Sri Nityananda, in the Madhya-lila, called "The Journey through the Northern Country".

Notes

  1. A Sanskrit shloka badly corrupted in both copies ("kalamvita mukkikaṁ … yata padāśraẏa vidhyata"). The first line is restored as the well-known pranama mantra nityanandam aham vande karne lambita-mauktikam; the second is understood as yat-padashraya-viryatah … taret samsara-ghorabdhim.
  2. The word "mālāte" ("in garlands"?) is unclear. Kamakhya is the goddess worshipped in Assam; songs of Mahipala (a king of the Pala dynasty), Yogipala and Bhogipala were popular in Bengal (cf. the Chaitanya Bhagavata).
  3. Bhot: coarse woollen blankets from Bhutan; chat: jute sacking.
  4. Kiriti ("the diademed one") is Arjuna; the allusion is to his weapon that stupefies enemies.
  5. The copies have "nivṛtti / nivunti"; the sense is conjectural.
  6. A prahara is about three hours; a danda about 24 minutes.
  7. Keshava Chhatri (Keshava Khan) was an official of Husain Shah, sultan of Gauda; Ramakeli is a place near the Gauda capital where Chaitanya met Rupa and Sanatana. His son is named in the text as Durlabha Chhatri.
  8. Trikachchha: a dhoti tucked in three places, a householder's garment, as opposed to a sannyasi's robe.
  9. The copies have "kheli / geli"; read as "meli", "meeting together".
  10. Names of Bengali sweets: manda, manohara, pera (milk sweets), khaja (flaky pastry), kshirisa (of thickened milk), ganga-jali, khandasar (a kind of sugar), pheni (thin sweet vermicelli), nabat (sugar-candy).
  11. "Sri Charana" ("the holy feet") is a respectful designation of the Lord; the copies have "stīcarana vijaẏa / śrīcarana [va]ẏa".
  12. The copies have "navarūpa" here and "narakūpa / narakapa" in couplet 100; "nararūpa", "human form", is adopted.
  13. Devottara: land endowed to a deity, exempt from revenue; the patta is the deed of grant.
  14. Sripat: a holy place, the seat of a Vaishnava teacher.
  15. Radha (rāṛha) is the region west of the Ganges (West Bengal) in which Ekachakra lies.
  16. Bankima-deva (Bankima Raya) is the deity of Krishna with the flute at Ekachakra.
  17. The copies have "kardtha keśara / katha keśava … aṅga"; read as "kadamva keśara aṅga" — the image of hair standing on end like the filaments of a kadamba flower.
  18. "madhukulā paẏaḥkulā" — probably dishes of kul (jujube) fruit with honey and with milk.
  19. The opening of the second line ("nipana haila") is corrupt; translated according to the sense.
  20. Virachandrapur is a village near Ekachakra (today Birchandrapur, Birbhum district).
  21. Sri Kundala is unidentified; probably a holy place or deity in Radha.
  22. The line is unclear; translated according to the sense, with the insertion in brackets.
  23. Padmavati is Nityananda's mother.
